text:
Bitcoin plunged to a $64,400–$64,700 channel during the Asian session, dragged by a hawkish pivot from the Federal Reserve. Chair Kevin Warsh's decision to hold rates at 3.50%–3.75% accompanied an aggressively revised dot plot, destroying near-term rate cut expectations and cementing the Crypto Fear & Greed Index at 22.

Despite macro headwinds, institutional tokenization quietly advances. European asset manager Amundi launched tokenized share classes for its Money Market Fund, signaling that infrastructure development remains detached from spot volatility.

In TradFi, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) surged to a two-month high of 100.31, acting as a massive gravitational pull on risk assets. Although Asian equities rallied on an interim U.S.-Iran peace framework, U.S. markets face a daunting liquidity landscape. Until the DXY breaks its uptrend, Bitcoin will struggle to overcome the oppressive weight of rising traditional yields and a structurally stronger dollar.
